clue.text: Military uniforms for women in prison

definitions.note: a phrase for the female officer who guards women prisoners

parts.note: military matters are those of war
uniforms are a form of dress

explanation.surface: A question of what military-style uniforms female inmates should wear.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests clothing issued to prisoners; in fact the definition is the female warder who looks after them.
explanation.definitionFit: A wardress is the female equivalent of a warder, an officer guarding inmates in a women's jail.

clue.text: It sounds as if having meals is a protection from rain

indicators.note: what follows is a word heard rather than read, so its spelling may change

parts.note: whether can introduce a supposition, akin to 'as if'
boarding means being supplied with meals, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: A claim that eating is a kind of shelter from the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: WHETHER is heard as WEATHER; board means meals, as in 'full board'.
explanation.definitionFit: Weatherboarding is overlapping timber cladding on outside walls that sheds water.

clue.text: Replay concerned with a bit of cricket

parts.note: re means concerning or regarding
a run is the unit of scoring in cricket

explanation.surface: A repeat showing of some cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A rerun is a repeated broadcast or contest.

clue.text: Offspring of violence produced by farmer

indicators.note: offspring OF violence puts the violence first, the issue after it

parts.note: rape is a violent sexual assault; here also a crop plant
seed means offspring, descendants

explanation.surface: A grim phrase about a child born of an assault, then a farm product.
explanation.walkthrough: Rape is also a crop grown for oil, which is how a farmer produces it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapeseed is the oil-bearing seed of the rape plant, an arable crop.

clue.text: Now mother has gone the dog is, obstinate

indicators.note: once mother has left, her letters are removed from the dog

parts.note: a mastiff is a large powerful dog breed
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: With mum away, the family dog has become stubborn.
explanation.definitionFit: Stiff can mean unbending or stubborn in attitude.

clue.text: Half-loves becoming cleaner

indicators.note: becoming means turning into something else, so these letters change their order

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O, so two loves give two Os

explanation.surface: Loving only half-heartedly turns someone into a cleaner person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becoming' rearranges HALF with OO (two loves, love being nil in tennis scoring).
explanation.definitionFit: A loofah is a dried gourd sponge used for scrubbing the body in the bath.

clue.text: Dedicated person is flattened

definitions.meaning: someone devoted to a religious life, often a lay member attached to a monastery
squashed at the poles, as a spheroid is

explanation.surface: A devoted person who has been squashed.
explanation.definitionFit: Oblate is a noun for a person dedicated to religious service, and an adjective for a sphere flattened at the poles.

clue.text: Pole needed to get flow ers over the river

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece placed over another comes first

parts.note: the text splits one word in two; flags are irises, plants of wet ground
the Taff is a river in Wales flowing through Cardiff

explanation.surface: A pole is required to fetch flowers from across the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The flags are irises, not banners; the Taff is the river through Cardiff.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagstaff is a pole from which a flag is flown.

clue.text: Let England share broadcast opera

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are dispersed into another order

explanation.surface: Let the whole nation enjoy a televised opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges 'Let England share'.
explanation.definitionFit: Humperdinck's 1893 fairy-tale opera based on the Grimm story.

clue.text: Ensure-it is consumed when hungry

indicators.note: the letters are used up and remade, broken down into a new order

explanation.surface: Make certain the food is eaten when appetite strikes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is consumed' rearranges the letters of 'Ensure-it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Esurient is a literary word for greedy or ravenous.

clue.text: Adult spoils and wastes away

parts.note: A is the film-classification abbreviation for adult
spoils of war or victory are trophies

explanation.surface: A grown-up spoils things and lets them waste away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoils' reads as a verb but is the noun for prizes taken in victory.
explanation.definitionFit: To atrophy is to wither or degenerate through disuse.

clue.text: Become acquainted with king by name

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's legendary king of Britain

explanation.surface: Getting to know a monarch by his name.
explanation.definitionFit: To learn something is to come to know it or gain familiarity with it.

clue.text: Searches for somewhere which no longer exists

definitions.meaning: looks for, seeks out, as a verb
The short form of Huntingdonshire, an English county abolished in 1974

explanation.surface: Looking for a place that has vanished.
explanation.walkthrough: Huntingdonshire, abbreviated Hunts, was a county of England merged into Cambridgeshire in 1974.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunts is a verb meaning seeks, and also the abbreviation for a vanished English county.

clue.text: Sample of a setter being wrong

indicators.note: the words placed before this are wrong, that is jumbled into a different order

explanation.surface: A trial piece from a crossword compiler who has made a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being wrong' rearranges the letters of 'of a setter'.
explanation.definitionFit: A foretaste is an early sample or preview of something to come.

clue.text: Cut back like a ditch in the grass

indicators.note: the ditch goes inside the grass, as 'in' states

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass of wet places
a trench is a long narrow ditch

explanation.surface: Describing a scene of a trench dug through tall grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like a ditch' reads as a description of the cutting, but it only supplies the ditch; 'in' is the container signal and 'the grass' gives the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrench is to reduce or economise, so retrenched means reduced or pared down.

clue.text: After heat I act right for a month"

indicators.note: what follows comes after the heat unit in the assembled word

parts.note: a therm is a unit of heat
to do is to act or perform

explanation.surface: Instructions for behaving properly once the hot weather comes.
explanation.walkthrough: Thermidor, 'heat-gift', was the eleventh month of the French Revolutionary calendar.
explanation.definitionFit: A summer month in the calendar of the French Republic.

clue.text: Approach which makes, food, ready to eat

parts.note: chips are fried potato food
hot food is cooked and ready to serve

explanation.surface: A recipe line about fried food served hot.
explanation.walkthrough: In golf an approach is a stroke to the green, often a short lofted one.
explanation.definitionFit: A short lofted golf stroke onto the green is an approach shot.

clue.text: This is one story, but two could be taken either way

definitions.text: This is one story, but two could be taken either way

parts.words: This is one story, but two could be taken either way
parts.note: one tale of heroes; the plural of the word is a palindrome, reading the same in both directions

explanation.surface: A tale which, doubled, is ambiguous.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural, SAGAS, reads the same backwards, which is what 'taken either way' points to.
explanation.definitionFit: A saga is a long story, originally a Norse heroic narrative.

clue.text: Dream go crazy, being a character

indicators.note: crazy means wild or deranged, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: the anagram fodder as printed, which needs an extra I in front of it to give the right letters

explanation.surface: Someone dreaming of going mad, being an eccentric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' rearranges the fodder, but 'Dream go' is short of an I as given; with I added, the letters make the answer. 'character' means a written symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideogram is a written symbol standing for an idea, as in Chinese script.

clue.text: Having lost his head, the amateur is finished

indicators.note: losing the head means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: an amateur is literally a lover of an activity, from Latin amator

explanation.surface: An amateur who has panicked and is now done for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having lost his head' removes the first letter L. Amateur means lover, from the Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: Over means ended or completed, as in 'the game is over'.

clue.text: Do deeds fit to provide material for the bards

definitions.note: metonymy: a gathering of Welsh poets

indicators.note: the letters of the words before are raw material to be worked into something new

explanation.surface: Perform heroic feats worth singing about by poets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to provide material for' says the letters of 'Do deeds fit' are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An eisteddfod is a Welsh festival of poetry and music, originally a congress of bards.

clue.text: Agreement for a second among the workers

indicators.note: the second goes among, that is inside, the workers

parts.note: a trade union is a body of workers
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A brief accord reached among the staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Unison means complete accord, all acting together.

clue.text: Be nostalgic about cars before church

parts.note: re is Latin-derived for about or concerning
Minis are a classic British small car
CE is the Church of England abbreviation

explanation.surface: Someone getting sentimental over old cars before going to church.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mini is a small British car made from 1959.
explanation.definitionFit: To reminisce is to recall past times fondly.

clue.text: Run in next race

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A competitor will run in the coming race.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an extra is a run not scored off the bat, such as a wide or bye.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket term for a run credited without the bat.

clue.text: Present the chest after a hundred has been removed

indicators.note: something taken away means the letter is deleted from the word

parts.note: a coffer is a strongbox or chest
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A gift of the chest once a hundred pounds has been taken out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a noun or adjective; it is the verb meaning to proffer.
explanation.definitionFit: To offer something is to present or proffer it.

clue.text: Beginner enters number for meals

definitions.note: a noun used loosely in the plural; meal is coarsely ground grain

indicators.note: the beginner goes into the number

parts.note: four is a number
L is a learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A novice joins a party of four for dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: L stands for learner on British L-plates; 'meals' means ground grain, not dinners.
explanation.definitionFit: Meal is ground grain, which is essentially what flour is.

clue.text: River which needs to try to make work

indicators.note: what this river lacks is this word, so it is missing from the longer one

parts.note: industry is hard work or diligence

explanation.surface: A river that must make an effort to get things done.
explanation.walkthrough: The river plus TRY makes INDUSTRY (work), so 'needs' signals that TRY has been taken away.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indus is a major river flowing through Pakistan.

clue.text: The furthest away may be disposed to muster too

indicators.note: disposed means arranged or set out, so the letters are put in another order

explanation.surface: Distant troops might be willing to assemble too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be disposed' rearranges 'muster too'.
explanation.definitionFit: Outermost means farthest from the centre.

clue.text: Bit of grammar which helps to make a stranger understand the language

indicators.note: the two words each contribute part of the run, so together they hold the answer

explanation.surface: Learning grammar helps a foreigner grasp the language.
explanation.walkthrough: The run lies across 'stranGER UNDerstand'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gerund is a verbal noun ending in -ing, a grammatical form.

clue.text: Where to get something soothing before an exam

parts.note: balm is a soothing ointment
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: Advice on where to find a remedy for pre-exam nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: Balmoral is the royal family's castle in Scotland, a place, hence 'Where'.
explanation.definitionFit: A place-name: the Scottish royal residence on Deeside.
